decision: REVISED per lock-review: enforcement is NOT warn-by-default. During feature implementation, evidence-class mismatch is advisory (warn). At PLAN CLOSE, product-class plans (goal_type in {parity, new_feature, migration, incident} -- the objective-contract-required set) with declared consumer journeys BLOCK unless each declared consumer outcome is satisfied, explicitly deferred as a non-goal, or operator-dispositioned. Internal substrate plans (goal_type in {mechanical, infra, refactor}) are advisory unless opted in.
rationale: A warn-only readiness gate cannot prevent its own failure mode ('plan completes though the consumer outcome was not proven'). Mapping block-by-default onto the objective-contract-required goal_type set (there is no product/readiness goal_type) gives teeth on product-class plans while keeping low false-positive risk on substrate plans.

decision: F005 handles consumer=both: a journey declaring consumer=both requires a satisfying consumer-surface capture for BOTH families (human AND agent); a missing family yields consumer_outcome_unproven and blocks (product-class).
rationale: Sufficiency finding (high): F001 permitted consumer=both but F005 only described human/agent enforcement, leaving both ambiguous.

decision: Reconcile degraded-vs-real (the 'real-or-honestly-degraded' promise vs F005's >=1-real requirement): the >=1 real (non-seeded) requirement is about JOURNEY EXECUTION provenance (the journey runs on the real surface, data_provenance != seeded). A required_data_source honestly degraded (availability=unavailable, F004) WITHIN such a real journey still satisfies; only a journey that is entirely seeded / substrate-only / typed-skip-only fails.
rationale: Sufficiency finding (high, parity_gap): contract+F004 said honest degradation passes while F005 demanded a real journey — contradictory until execution-provenance is separated from data-source availability.

decision: Deferral and disposition are STRUCTURED, not prose: deferral = an objective_contract non_goal entry naming {journey, consumer}; operator disposition = a consumer_outcome_dispositions[] record {journey, consumer, reason, dispositioned_by, at}. F005 validation requires these structured fields; prose alone never satisfies the close gate.
rationale: Sufficiency finding (medium): F005 relied on deferral/disposition with no structured fields to distinguish them from ordinary prose.

decision: Round-2 sufficiency: the close BLOCK is a DETERMINISTIC pre-flip gate consumer_outcome_gate in completion_gate.close_plan, invoked before the active->completed flip and INDEPENDENT of the codex F0 cluster triage (whose only blocking triage is child_plan); completion_auditor's consumer_outcome_unproven is the advisory surface only.
rationale: Finding (critical): auditing and plan close are separate concerns — a finding file alone would not guarantee product-class close is blocked, since _decide_blocking keys on cluster triage (child_plan) + envelope status, not gap_class. A deterministic gate pins the real enforcement seam.

decision: Round-2 sufficiency + operator correction: the experience-readiness gate ACTIVATES when ANY of (a) plan.md frontmatter experience_readiness_opt_in:true, (b) the objective_contract declares any journey with a consumer set, or (c) goal_type is product-class {parity,new_feature,migration,incident} OR plan metadata marks product/migration/readiness/ux/consumer-facing delivery. opt_in is NOT the sole activation path — product claims cannot dodge the gate by omitting the frontmatter field. Substrate-only internal plans with no consumer journeys (and not opted-in, not product-marked) no-op. experience_readiness_active() is the pure activation predicate; enforcement_posture() returns block for product-class/consumer-journey-bearing active plans, advisory for a substrate plan opted-in with no journeys, noop otherwise.
rationale: Operator correction before round-3 (2026-06-15): an opt-in-only activation lets product/consumer-facing claims silently bypass the readiness gate if someone forgets the frontmatter field — a safety hole. Multi-trigger activation (opt-in OR consumer-journey OR product goal_type/metadata) closes it while still no-op'ing pure substrate plans.

decision: Round-3 enforcement fix: resolve the activation/posture contradiction. ANY consumer-journey-bearing plan blocks an unproven consumer outcome regardless of the opt_in flag (activation trigger (b)); the advisory/warn path is ONLY a substrate plan that opted in but declares NO consumer journeys. The earlier 'substrate without flag only warns' wording (self-inflicted in 002 D022 test-10) is removed.
rationale: Finding (critical): test-10 'without flag only warns' contradicted trigger-(b) 'consumer-journey-bearing blocks'. A consumer journey is a real consumer claim; it blocks. Warn is reserved for opt-in-for-visibility on journey-less substrate plans.

decision: Round-3 enforcement fix: a product-class plan (or product-metadata-marked) that declares NO consumer journey emits a no_consumer_journey_declared advisory finding rather than silently passing the gate — the gate activates but has a consumer outcome obligation to surface.
rationale: Finding (high): product-class activation with no declared journey was a dodge path (gate active, nothing to evaluate). Flagging the absence closes it.
